item.text: {"code":"","conclusion":"1985 had the highest observed absolute median wealth gap among respondents with ever_jailed = 1: male median 1,000 versus female median 0, a gap of 1,000 supplied wealth units. Both medians were 0 in 1990 and 1996, yielding zero gaps. All three years included the same 289 respondents (37 female, 252 male), with no reported missing or invalid wealth, sex, or incarceration indicators; complete-case results were identical. Evidence roots: a66811b823fe7cdee4915ebca348542b36b51eb9578c45379314d39554a50841 (analysis) and 477078f3710344aa24408729347128a62bc7a5a06bc33ded6a8ebdad72d1396f (profile).","limitations":["Both executions succeeded, but validator verification covers execution receipts and input identity only, not scientific validity.","The indicator measures being jailed during 1985–1994, not lifetime incarceration or incarceration before each wealth measurement. Gender is represented by recorded binary sex labels.","These are unweighted descriptive sample medians, with only 37 female respondents; no significance test or population uncertainty estimate is provided, and causal conclusions are unsupported.","Negative and zero wealth values were retained; undocumented sentinel codes cannot be excluded. Inflation adjustment and cross-year composite comparability are undocumented.","The ranking concerns absolute median differences across the three supplied years; zero median gaps do not establish equality of wealth distributions."]}
